source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to formalize some known mathematics of its own choice that is absent from both Mathlib and LeanFrontier, with no prescribed subject. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT screened several classical candidates against live LeanFrontier and Mathlib, rejected Chebyshev's sum inequality, Popoviciu's variance inequality, Erdős-Szekeres, Beatty and the Gregory-Leibniz series because Mathlib already contains them, and selected the classical Hornich-Hlawka inequality for real inner-product spaces. Searches of LeanFrontier and current Mathlib found no theorem under Hornich-Hlawka/Hlawka or an equivalent quadrilateral-inequality formulation. The theorem states ||x+y||+||y+z||+||z+x|| <= ||x||+||y||+||z||+||x+y+z||. The proof is the standard one: use the inner-product norm-square identity relating the four single/total norms to the three pair-sum norms; after multiplying the target difference by the nonnegative sum of the four right-hand norms, rewrite it as a sum of three products, each product nonnegative by two applications of the triangle inequality. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the target and authored the Lean statement and proof; the human did not choose or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
